Quahadi

Quahadi, also written Quahada in the selected historical account, is a Comanche band/division reading route. The Texas report situates its history in the Llano Estacado while emphasizing the wider fluidity of Comanche band organization. Hosmer’s Quanah Parker biography follows one leader from resistance on the plains into later reservation-era work. These are starting readings about a particular historical community and individual, not a claim that one leader represented every Comanche group or that all families shared one experience.

Quanah Parker, Quahadi Comanche leader, in an albumen portrait
Unidentified photographer. Quanah Parker albumen portrait, Heritage Auctions, 2013 lot 44190 / Wikimedia Commons. Public domain in the United States per Commons media notice; exact photograph date and first publication unknown.

Source & image record ↗ · Public domain in the United States — Commons media-specific PD-US notice; creator/publication date not established

The exact Commons file and its linked 2013 Heritage Auctions lot both identify the sitter as Quanah Parker; the auction body describes the albumen portrait and states there is no photographer's identification. Brian C. Hosmer's actual TSHA entry explicitly identifies Quanah with the Quahada Comanche; this supplies the band-specific historical connection, rather than geography or appearance. The complete 1180-by-1474 original JPEG from this independent Commons/Heritage source was downloaded once and visually inspected. It is a head-and-torso portrait against a cloth backdrop and a different image from the blocked LOC full-length standing portrait; no LOC pixels, mirror or endpoint was used. Commons assigns a media-specific U.S. public-domain notice but warns that the creator and publication date matter outside the United States; those facts are not silently invented. The approximate 1890 date is attributed to Commons and is not independently established by the auction description. Retain the source's preexisting digitization and dark lower edge; no new restoration, crop, colorization, retouching or generated pixels. The portrait identifies one historical leader, not all Quahadi people or their current government. These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

A particular historical route on the plains

The consulted report identifies Quahadi within Comanche band history and associates the name with the Llano Estacado. Its discussion of changing local bands and divisions helps readers keep a historical regional label separate from a precise boundary or present governmental jurisdiction.

Read the sources [1] Texas Department of Transportation

02

One leader across changing institutions

Hosmer’s account describes Quanah’s leadership among the Quahadas and his later involvement in ranching, leases and other institutions under reservation conditions. Those choices should be read as a particular leader’s responses to pressure, rather than proof of unanimous consent or a complete account of family and community priorities.

Read the sources [2] Texas State Historical Association / Handbook of Texas Online; Brian C. Hosmer

TxDOT Tribal Histories: Comanche Nation Research Report — selected pages ↗

Texas Department of Transportation. 2021. TxDOT Tribal Histories: Comanche Nation Research Report. December. Selected pages.

Publication: 2021-12

A chronological Texas synthesis prepared with the Nation’s historic-preservation office. Selected text supports a regional starting guide; its sources, dates and interpretations still need comparison.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Downloaded actual72-page PDF and read selected text: printed/PDFpp3,6–10,35–36,50–54. Map images and cited originals were not inspected; no sensitive-site locations or ceremonial instructions are reproduced.

Review recorded: October 26, 2026

Access status: Public text inspected

Access note: Browser fetch timed out; official file downloaded successfully and selected pages extracted with pypdf. Review is textual, not visual inspection of illustrations. Internal chronology includes Texas annexation as1846 onp36 and a March1882 visit after1891 onp54; these dates are not adopted. Evaluative claims about individual leaders and reported historical counts remain outside this synthesis. Consultation does not make every statement independently verified.

Quanah Parker — selected Quahadi leadership and reservation-era account ↗

A biographical introduction to Quanah’s Quahadi leadership and later economic and institutional work. The guide keeps disputed early biography and sweeping judgments apart from its selected historical orientation. One leader’s life is not the complete history of Quahadi families or all Comanche governments.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual full main body and bibliography read, web lines6–34. Synthesis uses Quahadi leadership and reservation-era ranching/institutional passages11–23. Contested birth and early family chronology, numerical casualty/wealth claims, religious details and burial information are not repeated; original family accounts and cited books remain unreviewed.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026

Access note: Public HTML main body inspected. Bibliography points to further works; those underlying publications and original records were not read here.
